run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three requested queries were executed against the three app-280 log indices in Elasticsearch; in each case the field named in the request does not exist in that index, and a re-run against the index's actual severity field produced a count. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no 'level' field (mapped fields: @timestamp date, message text, service keyword, severity keyword); term level=ERROR returned 0 documents, and term severity=ERROR returned 10. Total documents in that index inside the 2026-10-24T19:40:13Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z @timestamp window were 16, with severity buckets ERROR=10 and INFO=6. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has no 'level' field; its severity field is the integer severity_num. terms level=[ERROR,FATAL] returned 0; terms severity_num=[5,6] returned 8, and the sample documents identify 5 as [ERROR] and 6 as [FATAL] (severity_num 3 is [INFO]). (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no @timestamp field at all — its only time-like field is ingest_ts, mapped as keyword, so the tool applied no time filter. The requested range on @timestamp with level=ERROR returned 0; a lexicographic range on ingest_ts for 2026-11-23 with level=ERROR returned 7 (with 5 more ERROR documents dated 2026-11-22). Counts are document counts from these small indices as queried, not unique events, and 'today' was taken as 2026-11-23, the date of the authorized window end.

claims.text: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); it has no 'level' field.

As requested, term { level: "ERROR" } on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 documents (1 shard successful, 0 failed) inside the @timestamp window 2026-10-24T19:40:13Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z; the field 'level' is not in that index's mapping, so no document can match it.
Re-run on the correct field: term { severity: "ERROR" } on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 10 documents over 2026-10-24T19:40:13Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z.

For app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the whole 16-document set (2026-11-03 samples) aggregates as severity ERROR=10 and INFO=6 with sum_other_doc_count 0, consistent with the 10 returned by the severity=ERROR term query.
app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it has no 'level' field and no keyword severity field.
As requested, terms { level: ["ERROR","FATAL"] } on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 documents over 2026-10-24T19:40:13Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z.

The severity_num values actually present in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 are 5 (6 documents), 3 (5 documents) and 6 (2 documents); sample messages show "[ERROR] DB timeout N" with severity_num 5, "[FATAL] Disk full N" with severity_num 6, and "[INFO] healthcheck N" with severity_num 3.

Re-run on the correct field: terms { severity_num: [5,6] } on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 8 documents over 2026-10-24T19:40:13Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z (6 with severity_num 5 sev, 2 with severity_num 6), all from svc order-280.
app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it has no date-typed field and no @timestamp field, and the tool reported time_filter applied=false for it.

As requested, bool(range @timestamp 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z, term level=ERROR) on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0, and the tool noted "No matched index maps a date field, so no time filter was applied"; @timestamp does not exist in this index's mapping, which is why the range matched nothing.

Re-run on the correct time-like field: lexicographic range on keyword ingest_ts (2026-11-23T00:00:00 to 2026-11-23T23:59:59.999) plus term level=ERROR on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 7 documents.

All 16 documents of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 were readable: level buckets ERROR=12 and INFO=4, and ingest_ts values span 2026-11-22T08:01:00–2026-11-22T08:05:00 (ERROR, messages "err yest 1"–"err yest 5"), 2026-11-23T08:01:00–2026-11-23T08:07:00 (ERROR, "err today 1"–"err today 7") and 2026-11-23T09:01:00–2026-11-23T09:04:00 (INFO, "info today 1"–"info today 4").

"Today" was interpreted as the UTC calendar date 2026-11-23 (the date of the authorized window end, 2026-11-23T19:40:13Z); the documents whose messages say "err today"/"info today" indeed carry ingest_ts values on 2026-11-23, which is consistent with but does not itself define that date convention.

The numeric severity scale in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 is inferred from message prefixes (3=[INFO], 5=[ERROR], 6=[FATAL]) rather than from a documented mapping; no document with severity_num 4 was observed in this index, so the meaning of that value is unknown.

gaps: The requester did not define "today" or a timezone; the answer for question 3 uses UTC date 2026-11-23 (50 documents' worth of context: 7 ERROR on that date), matching the authorized window end 2026-11-23T19:40:13Z.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-typed field: ingest_ts is keyword, so the tool applied no time filter and the returned counts cannot be proven to fall inside the incident window; the range was lexicographic on the keyword string.
Counts for app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 and app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 were limited to @timestamp 2026-10-24T19:40:13Z–2026-11-23T19:40:13Z by the tool; any documents outside that window are unknown.
Counts are Elasticsearch document totals for these small indices (16, 13 and 16 documents), not unique events, and a document not returned/aggregated outside these queries is unknown.
The severity_num-to-label mapping for app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 is inferred from msg text; no authoritative severity mapping was read.
Mappings and document counts reflect the cluster at query time (observed_at 2026-11-23T19:40:16Z–19:40:31Z) and cannot prove what the indices contained earlier.
next_steps: Confirm the intended date and timezone for "today" before reusing the question-3 count of 7.
If historical counts are needed, confirm whether any date-typed timestamp exists (or can be added) for app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, since ingest_ts is only a keyword string.
Confirm the numeric severity convention (3/5/6) used by the app-280 log shipper if exact ERROR+FATAL semantics matter.
